root.label: Strings and string_view
root.note: An owning buffer versus a borrowed window onto characters.

children.label: std::string guarantees
children.note: Contiguous, null-terminated storage with vector-like growth and invalidation.

children.label: Contiguous storage
children.note: data() works with any pointer-and-length API.

children.label: Null terminator (C++11)
children.note: data()[size()] is readable and equals the null character; writing another value is undefined.

children.label: Invalidation
children.note: Non-const members other than operator[], at, data, front, back and begin/end may invalidate.

children.label: Small string optimization
children.note: An implementation habit, not a standard promise.

children.label: Inline short strings
children.note: libstdc++ holds 15 chars, libc++ 22 on 64-bit; the standard names neither.

children.label: Pointers move with object
children.note: Pointers into a short string point into the string object itself.

children.label: Modern string API
children.note: Newer members that say what you mean.

children.label: resize_and_overwrite (C++23)
children.note: Skips zero-fill; every character you report must be written, and the callable must not throw.

children.label: npos idioms
children.note: npos is the unsigned maximum, so npos + 1 wraps to zero.

children.label: starts_with, contains
children.note: C++20 starts_with and ends_with, C++23 contains, avoid npos comparisons.

children.label: std::string_view
children.note: A non-owning pointer and length.

children.label: Not null-terminated
children.note: data()[size()] is not guaranteed; slices continue into the original text.

children.label: Cheap slicing
children.note: substr, remove_prefix and remove_suffix are O(1) and copy nothing.

children.label: Dangling from temporaries
children.note: A view built from s + "x" outlives the temporary and is undefined to read.

children.label: Borrowed range
children.note: A string_view is both a view and a borrowed range.

children.label: Conversions and parameters
children.note: Implicit one way, explicit the other.

children.label: string to view implicit
children.note: A conversion operator on string; free and cannot fail.

children.label: view to string explicit
children.note: A constructor that allocates; assignment and += from a view still work.

children.label: Choosing parameter types
children.note: string_view for read-only text, string to store it, const char* if terminator needed.

children.label: Literals and traits
children.note: Suffixes and the template behind the names.

children.label: "x"s and "x"sv
children.note: The s suffix makes a string, sv a view with known length, in std::literals.

children.label: char_traits
children.note: Supplies comparison and copy; different traits give different types.

children.label: No view + view
children.note: There is no operator+ for two views; C++26 adds string and view mixes.
